title: Adaptive Micro-session Shimming to Reduce KV Hotspots in Streaming Chat
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: We observe periodic KV cache pressure and GPU memory fragmentation during high-concurrency streaming chat workloads caused by many short-lived micro-sessions (1-3 token turns). These micro-turns arrive staggered and create KV hot spots and frequent small allocations on the GPU slab allocator, increasing tail latency and token-cost per request. Existing session-merging heuristics either wait too long (hurting latency) or aggressively conflate unrelated contexts (hurting correctness).

Proposal: Implement an adaptive 'micro-session shimming' layer in the continuous batcher. The shim is a lightweight per-request sampler that delays dispatch by a configurable micro-window (0-30ms) for micro-turns and optionally injects benign token-padding metadata to align token boundaries across sessions for efficient KV packing. Key components: 1) Micro-turn classifier (turn length + recency + priority) to decide if a request is shim-eligible. 2) Adaptive micro-window controller driven by observed KV slot utilization and tail-latency SLOs. 3) Shim encoding that attaches a zero-cost alignment marker to allow safe prefix coalescing without changing model outputs (uses function-calling framing where available). 4) Integrated GPU slab coalescer that groups aligned KV slots and compacts free fragments before dispatch. 5) Backpressure rules: high-priority or deadline-bound requests bypass shimming.

Acceptance criteria: 1) 95th percentile token latency for streaming completions improves by >=15% on internal benchmark for mixed micro-session workloads at 80% utilization. 2) GPU slab fragmentation metric drops by >=20% (measured via allocator free-run ratio). 3) No measurable regression in output correctness for 10k eval prompts (paraphrase + intent tests). 4) End-to-end cost per token reduced by >=8% on target workload.

Implementation plan: Phase 1 (spike) - prototype sampler + micro-window and run offline trace-driven simulator to tune thresholds (2 weeks). Phase 2 - integrate shim encoding and safe coalescing in runtime (3 weeks). Phase 3 - GPU slab coalescer and KV packing changes + nightly canary rollout to dedicated pool with synthetic load (2 weeks). Phase 4 - ramp to hosted region with experiment and automated rollback on quality regressions (2 weeks).

Trade-offs and risks: Shimming introduces small additional latency for some requests; mitigated by adaptive bypass for low-latency SLOs. The shim encoding must be strictly no-op for model semantics; we will validate with model-agnostic framing and run full eval suites. GPU slab coalescing increases allocator complexity and risk of new fragmentation patterns; plan is to gate behind rollout flag and monitor fragmentation metrics closely.

Observability and telemetry: New metrics: shim_eligible_rate, shim_applied_rate, shim_delay_histogram, kv_slot_coalesces, slab_free_run_ratio, shim_bypass_count (by reason). Dashboards: streaming/shim/* and alerts on >2% drop in eval-quality or >10% increase in tail-latency.

Testing: unit tests for sampler logic, integration tests with mocked allocator, end-to-end benchmark harness using recorded production traces, and quality regression tests against eval suite.

Rollout strategy: default off. Deploy to dedicated dev pool -> internal canary -> 5% traffic in hosted with QA-monitor -> 25% -> 100% if metrics pass. Automatic rollback if customer_impact or eval_quality regresses beyond thresholds.
